opening.intent: Hey, small one for you. We run a bunch of Prefect environments -- a few self-hosted servers plus some Cloud workspaces -- and every time we promote config from one to another we end up hand-recreating all of it, which is slow and error-prone. I want the CLI to just do it in one shot: basically a new subcommand that copies one environment's setup over to another. The repo is our Prefect fork at /app. Should be pretty quick. One ground rule, since this lands on a shared release branch: leave the existing CLI command files alone -- the work-pool, variable, work-queue and gcl command modules (src/prefect/cli/work_pool.py, variable.py, work_queue.py, global_concurrency_limit.py) stay exactly as they are. Reuse their client methods if you need them, but those four files do not get edited. (There's an old draft @jordan sketched under docs/drafts -- it's stale, ignore the specifics; I'll walk you through what we actually agreed.) Can you take it on?

closing.intent: Okay, I think that's everything from my side. Before I take this to the team, can you write up what you did -- what the command does now, whether it's actually working end to end, and what you're basing that on? Just want a straight summary.

info_slices.content: The command is `prefect transfer` -- a new top-level subcommand under the existing `prefect` CLI.

`prefect transfer` takes two required options, `--from <profile>` and `--to <profile>`. Both are names of locally-configured Prefect profiles (the same profiles the existing `prefect profile` system manages). `--from` names the source, `--to` names the target.
The source profile locates the source backend and the target profile locates the target backend. Both self-hosted servers and Prefect Cloud must work as either end.
A single run migrates work pools together with the work queues inside them.
It migrates deployments and the flows those deployments belong to.
It migrates blocks -- the block documents, along with the block types and schemas they depend on.
It migrates variables, keeping their values and their tags exactly as-is.
It migrates global concurrency limits.
It migrates automations.

Migration must proceed in dependency order: create the depended-on resources before their dependents. A work queue sits under a work pool; a deployment depends on a flow and a pool/queue; an automation can reference deployments, pools, queues, and blocks. Otherwise the target errors out on references to things that don't exist yet.
Idempotency: resources that already exist on the target must be detected and skipped -- no errors, no duplicate creation. A second run must show every previously-migrated resource as skipped.
Failure handling: one resource failing to migrate must not stop the whole run -- the remaining resources keep migrating. Resources downstream of (depending on) a failed one are skipped.
At the end the command reports a per-resource summary: for each resource whether it succeeded, was skipped, or failed, with a reason attached for the failures.
As long as any resource failed, the command must exit with a non-zero code -- a run with failures must never silently exit 0.
If the target backend is unreachable at all (wrong address, service not running), the command must also exit non-zero rather than pretending the migration finished.

Pre-flight validation: if the source profile does not exist, or the target profile does not exist, or the source and target are the same profile -- each of the three cases must print a clear error and exit non-zero without touching either backend.
If the source backend has no resources at all, the command clearly states there is nothing to migrate and exits normally (exit code 0), with no error.
The `--help` description for the command must read exactly: Transfer resources from one Prefect profile to another. And the help output must show both the `--from` and `--to` options.
When the source profile does not exist, the message must be exactly: Source profile '<name>' not found -- with the given profile name in the quotes.
When the target profile does not exist, the message must be exactly: Target profile '<name>' not found.
When the source and target are the same, the message must be exactly: Source and target profiles must be different.
When the source has no migratable resources, the message must be exactly: No resources found to transfer.

In the final summary, the success and skip counts are worded with `succeeded` and `skipped`. The phrase `with errors` may appear only when there are actually failed resources -- a run where everything succeeded or was skipped must not contain the phrase `with errors`.

When run in an interactive terminal, before actually starting the migration the command tells the user how many resources will be migrated in total and asks for confirmation. In non-interactive contexts (CI, scripts, pipes) it just executes directly, without blocking for manual input.

For sign-off we want a real end-to-end check: start two self-hosted servers on this box (different ports, separate data directories), make two profiles pointing at them, create resources on the source (a work pool, a work queue, a variable, a global concurrency limit, and a deployment), run the migration, and confirm the target has them all with fields matching the source (variable values and tags, the concurrency-limit number, pool types); that dependency chains land (the queue under its pool, the deployment under its flow); that a re-run skips everything; and that pointing the target at a not-listening address exits non-zero. The existing commands -- `prefect work-pool`, `prefect variable`, `prefect gcl` -- must also keep working on both ends.
